# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (use these instead of the source text)

## BOOK 1 — THE EMBLEMS OF FIDELITY (James Lane Allen, 1919, epistolary comedy)

**Characters:** Edward Blackthorne (famous elderly English novelist, King Alfred's Wood, Warwickshire; calls himself an elephant with a "proboscis" for praise); Beverley Sands (rising young American novelist, Cathedral Heights, New York; Kentuckian; age 27 in 1910; writes Kentucky novels); Benjamin "Ben" Doolittle (practical New York lawyer, 150 Broad St / Wall St, no imagination, "land-turtle", calls himself "Sal Blivvens" later; loves Polly); George Marigold (fashionable physician, Dr. G. M. Marigold); Claude Mullen (fashionable nerve-specialist, friend of Marigold, courts Polly); Rufus Kent (long-winded president of The Great Dipper club, "Nestor"); Noah Chamberlain (absent-minded botany professor, Seminole, N.C., "Approximations to Consciousness in Plants"; dies after falling down stairs); Clara Louise Chamberlain (his proud, sensitive daughter, later secretary); Phillips & Faulds, Burns & Bruce, Judd & Judd, Andy Peters (florists); Hodge (Blackthorne's stupid gardener, Latin-names obsessed, "Asplenium filix-faemina"); Tilly Snowden (Beverley's fiancée, "wild rose in a snow bank", "Slippery Elm" apartments; later marries Marigold); Polly Boles (Ben's sweetheart, Franklin Flats, later marries Mullen at City Hall, Jersey City); Anne Raeburn (Blackthorne's secretary, writes from England).

**Plot in order:**
1. May 1910: Blackthorne writes Sands praising his Kentucky novel; asks for Kentucky fern root-stocks for his fern bank (Corot/Turgenev/Nilsson anecdote; Turgenev: "That spot is all Russia!"). Offers to pay (£5 estimate). Sands replies warmly; mentions Shakespeare's bosom.
2. Blackthorne's May 22 letter: Hodge described (slabs, "Bishop's crooks", Latin names); visitors' tea and "fern walk"; invites Sands and wife to visit.
3. Sands to Tilly: jokes about marriage, England trip, Stonehenge tea; Tilly replies (Canaan and the strip of land; childhood friend of mother; she is "ill", consults Dr. Marigold; says she will take the Bulgar bacillus; wants to go to England, not as a mere guest).
4. Sands to Ben: "land-turtle" banter. Ben reply: "A poor, harmless tinker"; polecat metaphor; Ben's French quote "A chaque oiseau son nid est beau". Sands asks Ben for florist address; Ben recommends Phillips & Faulds.
5. Ben/Polly quarrel letters: Polly's Franklin Flats; Ben sends red roses; Polly's rival Dr. Mullen ("umbrageous society"). Tilly and Polly's bitter letters (Tilly: "Strictly Monogamous Women" banner; "Not Necessarily Monogamous!"; Polly: "domestic tea-kettle" insult).
6. Sands orders ferns from Phillips & Faulds (June 7, 1900 [sic] — actually 1910; check of $25 check); P&F accept (June 10).
7. June 15 letter to Blackthorne: "peach and bough" image; wooing persists.
8. Diary (June 16): Sands's fame spreads; club incident; reveals "There was no woodland scene and there were no ferns" — Sands invented a Kentucky spring scene from an August boyhood afternoon with a dry spring and sycamore.
9. **Part Second, May 1, 1911:** Blackthorne angry — ferns never arrived; accuses Sands of dishonesty; "Fidelity" emblem of fern. Sands replies coolly. Sands to Ben (May 13): Phillips & Faulds say order passed to Burns & Bruce (Dunkirk, Tenn.) who blamed P&F debts; Burns & Bruce refer to Noah Chamberlain (Seminole, N.C.). Sands orders from Chamberlain (May 25); Chamberlain says he is not a florist (May 29); daughter Clara's indignant letter ("peddle bulbs"); Sands mocks; Chamberlain: "Stop writing to me."; Clara: "viper".
10. Tilly quarrels with Sands over England; she breaks engagement; Ben's "Sal Blivvens"-style humour; Ben and Polly signed joint letter to Sands (June 15).
11. Tilly's letters to Dr. Marigold (she asks him for bills; tells her life story: six sisters, mother's suffrage protest, childhood pets; "long love is possible only when you love often"); Tilly sails-away letter; Tilly's June 21 letter to Sands ("I love you") and to Polly ("good-bye for life").
12. Polly's June 23–July 15: Dr. Mullen pursuit; Ben's proposal (July 15 Polly "Oh Ben"); Ben's "furnace-man" joke; Sands orders from Judd & Judd (July 16–23) who ship ferns; returned by Judd & Judd (Dec 27).
13. Chamberlain's Christmas letter (Dec 25): father died after fall; ferns a "fern list" caused it. Clara's appeal for job with Andy Peters (Jan 7, 1911 letters, 1912).
14. Ben's "Clara is sealing wax" letters; Sands visits Clara ("Sal Blivvens" letter from Ben to Blackthorne June 10, 1912; Blackthorne's reply June 21, 1912 — "cocksure", "Sal Blivvens", "Burns' 'To step aside is human'").
15. Hodge dies (Blackthorne's letter July 1912); Sands sails to England; Diary July 18, 1912: Tilly weds Marigold; Polly weds Mullen (Ocean Grove honeymoon); Ben goes to Kentucky to marry again ("Polly-like" woman); Sands sails for England; closing reflection: ferns as "Emblems of Fidelity".

**Key quoted phrases:** "Fidelity" fern emblem; "Le Génie Oblige"; "Expanding Scamp and the Shrinking Skin"; "Sal Blivvens"; "cocksure"; "Polly comes with the wedding clothes."

---

## BOOK 2 — A DEAD RECKONING (T. W. Speight, 1889, serialised in Chambers's Journal, 19 chapters)

**Characters:** Clara Brooke (née Danby? — no: Clara Danby, vicar's daughter; married Gerald; Mrs. Brooke, 22, brunette, black eyes); Gerald Brooke (26, fair, tall, owner of Beechley Towers, 14 miles from London; raised in Poland, learned pistol shooting; member of a Polish secret society "Supreme Tribunal"); Miss Jane Primby (Clara's aunt, fresh-coloured spinster, weak head, good heart; embroidery; "Major Pondicherry", "Count de Bonnechose"); Lady Fanny ("Fan") Dwyer (worldly matron, husband Algy, yachtsman, cruising in Mediterranean; her "modus vivendi"); Baron Otto von Rosenberg (ex-German diplomat, ~40–55, Beaulieu estate, pistol collector; victim); George Crofton (cousin of Gerald; dissipated, black hair, scar/gash on upper lip; loved Clara; disinherited by uncle; plots revenge; ends dead at Beechley, shot-disarmed); Stephanie Lagrange (circus "Queen of the Haute Ecole", Ventelli Circus; later Crofton's wife; secretly Picot's daughter); Henri Picot (boy, 8–9, blond curls, "cherub"; dies in January; Picot's son); Jules Picot (mountebank, drum and pipes, 43; former wife Marie; kills Von Rosenberg in revenge for seducing daughter Stephanie); Paul Karovsky (Russian, bearer of tribunal's death order, black hair, ivory complexion; later "personates" Gerald; leaves Gerald with "Remember!"); Bunce (pompous butler/majordomo); Dixon (groom); Margery Shook (orphan, ex-canal-barge girl, weird laugh, calls Gerald "Muster Geril"); Tom Starkie (Penrhyn Court, son of Sir John Starkie J.P.; friend who hides Gerald); Drumley (Superintendent of police, King's Harold); Roger Chamfrey (London friend, Yorkshire moor keeper); Timley (head-keeper, Yorkshire, "Mr. Davis" alias); Lucas (Gerald's mate, signalman); Slinkey, "Lardy Bill" (sham parson, gang members); Dr. Marigold/Mullen not in Book 2; Lord Leamington (jewel robbery target); Mr. Sturgess (London jeweller); Dr. King; Pringle (Von Rosenberg's man).

**Plot in order:**
- **Ch. I (24 April):** Six months since Gerald & Clara's marriage. Lady Fan explains her and Algy's "separate-meetings" marriage. Pistol practice (Gerald & Von Rosenberg). Picot and boy Henri, pistol-shots, Bunce insults them; Clara gives Henri cakes and a coin. Picot starts at Von Rosenberg's name.
- **Ch. II:** Gerald gives Von Rosenberg a gold-and-silver Indian (Nawab-given) pistol "for a few days". Walk in wood. Crofton appears, rants about lost love; Karovsky's card. Crofton alone pockets/smashes miniature of Gerald under heel. Clara finds fragments and locks them away. Gerald reveals Karovsky visited.
- **Ch. III:** Crofton had ridden with Stephanie to Beechley Arms, landlady Mrs. Purvis. Stephanie meets Henri in garden, learns his mother died; asks about "sister" (secret). Crofton finds her crying.
- **Ch. IV:** Karovsky visits Gerald; reveals Tribunal oath (8 years earlier, Warsaw); Gerald must assassinate Von Rosenberg (who betrayed Karovsky's brother's printing-press group, exiled to silver mines). Gerald refuses; Karovsky warns "Mrs. Brooke is very young to be left a widow." Says "Remember!"
- **Ch. V (end of June, ~10 weeks later):** Gerald writes warning letter to Baron; burns it. Dixon reports Von Rosenberg murdered in the "chalet" at Beaulieu. Margery reports police coming; murder weapon = Gerald's pistol; warrant for Gerald.
- **Ch. VI:** Tom Starkie reveals: pistol found; groom Pedley saw half-burnt letter; Gerald's alibi lacking. Tom advises flight. Clara begs Gerald to fly. Margery warns of police; they hide Gerald (Clara's plan: he is in the armour-suit in the hall).
- **Ch. VII:** Clara deceives Drumley (says Gerald left for Woodberry station); police search; Gerald hidden in armour (suit of mail) at foot of stair.
- **Ch. VIII:** Linden Villa, North-West London. Crofton & Stephanie married. Stephanie hears news of murder. Crofton plans to hire detective. Stephanie learns Von Rosenberg was her seducer (hints).
- **Ch. IX:** Gerald escapes to Penrhyn Court; Priest's Hole. Later sent to Yorkshire moor as "Mr. Davis", assistant keeper. Crofton finds him (groom recognition). Gerald then moves to London; meets Clara and Henri/Picot in Tottenham Court Road.
- **Ch. X:** Lodgings at No. 5 Pymm's Buildings, Soho, as "Mr. and Mrs. Stewart". Picot lives upstairs. Karovsky arrives; offers money; Gerald refuses. Police arrive; Karovsky offers to impersonate Gerald.
- **Ch. XI:** Karovsky taken as Gerald (sergeant). Crofton arrives, reveals he informed police; Picot (binds Crofton, gags with handkerchief, guard by Margery with revolver). Crofton burns rope, escapes.
- **Ch. XII (March, following year):** Crofton & Stephanie at Linden Villa; debts, card-cheating, racing losses. Crofton plots robbery of jewel box (£20,000, Lord Leamington's wedding gifts, 14 April). Stephanie threatens to leave.
- **Ch. XIII:** Cummerhays (northern England); Cinder Pit Junction; signalman James Maynard "Gentleman Jim" = Gerald under alias (Lady Fan's husband Algy obtained post). Lady Fan visits Clara (Margery's report). Margery spots Crofton at Varley's Cottage; Clara goes to see.
- **Ch. XIV:** Varley's Cottage (old murder site). Clara overhears plan: attack train at Cinder Pit; signalman bound. Margery fixes fog-signals (singles). Clara runs to warn Gerald; arrives too late; sees Slinkey in box.
- **Ch. XV:** Gerald bound to tree by "sham parson" Lardy Bill; Clara frees him (knife in outside pocket). Fog-signals stop train; gang caught; Crofton shoots Gerald (wound in arm). Crofton denounces Gerald.
- **Ch. XVI:** Cummerhays justice-room. Picot (in dock area) sees Clara and Gerald. Testimony by Sturgess, driver, Margery, Clara, Sergeant. Picot stands up and confesses killing Von Rosenberg.
- **Ch. XVII:** Picot's full confession (wife Marie, daughter Stephanie seduced by Baron; he shot Baron with Gerald's pistol after Baron struck him with whip). Picot remanded; dies in cell by poison (phial).
- **Ch. XVIII:** Picot's farewell letter to "Madame Brouke" (poison in heel of shoe; Henri died of accident; Picot's visions). Crofton escapes (file; rope with steel hooks); Lardy Bill disguised as "Colonel Crofton" visits him. Stephanie arrives; reads confession; learns her letter to father never arrived. Landlady reports Crofton escaped and Picot found dead.
- **Ch. XIX (Conclusion, six weeks later):** Gerald & Clara return to Beechley Towers; Miss Primby, Lady Fan, Tom Starkie, Margery ("own maid") present. Crofton shoots at Gerald through window; dark-cloaked figure (Karovsky) knocks gun away; Crofton says "Gerald Brooke, you have won the game!" and dies. Karovsky: Tribunal absolved Gerald.
- **END.**

**Key items/numbers:** £20,000 jewels; £300 reward; 28 June murder (Thursday); pistol = Nawab-gifted gold/silver Indian pistol; Crofton inheritance £5,000 legacy / Beechley Towers + £6,000 a year; Clara's father-in-law? (none); Penrhyn Court; Priest's Hole; Cinder Pit Junction; Varley's Cottage; Pymm's Buildings No. 5; Linden Villa; Beaulieu; King's Harold; Cummerhays; Greenholme; Mellingfield.
